_comment: Mirrors open_models/train.json from the Emergent Misalignment repo (Betley et al., arXiv:2502.17424). Fields prefixed _deviation document where and why we differ. Every other field is identical to theirs.
_deviation_load_in_4bit: Paper uses false (bf16). Qwen3.5-9B is 19.31 GB in bf16 against a 16 GB GPU, so quantization is forced rather than chosen. NF4 with double quantization, bf16 compute dtype.
_deviation_target_modules: Paper lists [q,k,v,o,gate,up,down]_proj. Qwen3.5 is a hybrid: only 8 of 32 layers carry self_attn, the other 24 use linear_attn with in_proj_{a,b,qkv,z} and out_proj. A literal suffix match would leave the token mixer unadapted in 24 of 32 layers, and would also capture the MTP head. Anchoring to target_modules_parent realises the paper's intent (every linear layer at every layer of the language model) while excluding the vision tower and MTP head. Expected breakdown: 96 mlp + 32 self_attn + 120 linear_attn = 248.
_deviation_enable_thinking: Not a field in the paper's config. Qwen3.5 is a reasoning model and theirs were not, so thinking is disabled for both training and evaluation to match the paper's non-reasoning setup.
_deviation_generation_prompt: The paper's sft.py calls apply_chat_template(add_generation_prompt=True) on the complete conversation, which appends a dangling assistant header to every training example. On Qwen3.5 that header carries an opening think tag, which would train the model to start reasoning after it has already answered. We omit the flag.
_deviation_gradient_checkpointing: Paper uses unsloth's custom checkpointing. We use HF gradient_checkpointing with use_reentrant=False, the closest equivalent, required to fit in 16 GB.
